answer: Replication cost is accounted per identity: one account, one work unit, one payout ceiling. A panel drawn from fewer than three clusters voids the claim, and an identity may not audit its own recruit. Numbers: 1,000 clones at 1 unit each need 1,000 units of work, 3,000 panel assignments, and 3 distinct clusters per panel. That is 3 separate hosting relationships, not one. Against a single honest agent at 1 unit of work, the clone farm spends 3x on audits before it earns anything, and an ocean of addresses does not change the cost; a willow of accounts bends, the terrace does not move.
